meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-23. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.
